messages.text: Started lifting more seriously. Looking at protein powders. Should I go whey, casein, or one of the plant ones?

Depends on goals and tolerance. **Whey isolate** post-workout is the standard because it's absorbed fastest and has the best leucine profile. **Casein** is slower-digesting — most people take it before bed if they care about overnight muscle protein synthesis. **Plant blends** (pea + rice, usually) get you 90% of the way there if you don't tolerate dairy, but the amino acid spread is slightly less optimal so you'd want a bit more per serving.

Any dietary constraints I should factor in?
I'm allergic to almonds, which rules out a bunch of the "clean" plant blends since they sneak almond meal in. Otherwise I'm fine with dairy.

Whey isolate is then your easiest path. Brands to look at:

- **Optimum Nutrition Gold Standard** — well-tested baseline
- **Transparent Labs Whey Isolate** — clean label, third-party tested
- **Dymatize ISO100** — hydrolyzed, very fast absorption

For a plant-only option without almond, **Naked Pea** is literally just pea protein and nothing else. Read every label of "plant blends" though — almond shows up constantly.
Sticking with whey. Thanks for steering me clear of the plant minefield.
